title: Throughput & Latency Workload Catalog and Micro-benchmark Playbook
author: Anika Rao
body:
Overview

Purpose: This catalog defines a small, reproducible set of micro- and macro-benchmarks, workload parameterizations, kernel-scheduler tuning matrices, and an operational playbook for running consistent performance characterization across Redwood’s serving runtime. Use this document to: triage regressions, validate kernel changes, gate releases, and build dashboards for long-term trend analysis.

Audience: runtime engineers, perf infra, SRE, model onboarding, and release managers.

Scope

- Micro-benchmarks (synthetic kernels): kernel latency, memcpy/pack/unpack, KV-cache hot/hard-miss paths.
- Model-shaped workloads: short prompt (<64 tokens), medium-gen (512 tokens), long-gen (2048+ tokens), and embeddings-heavy workloads.
- IO and network stress: multi-region cross-AZ routing and gateway-saturation tests.
- CI gating and release checklist for runtime/kernel changes.

Key Definitions and Metrics

- p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms (end-to-end request time measured at gateway).
- kernel_exec_ms (per-kernel wall time inside runtime).
- tokens_per_second (throughput for continuous-stream workloads).
- gpu_util_pct, mem_peak_mb, nvlink_bw_gbps (hardware-level counters).
- error_rate_pct (5xx+timeout rate observed during run).

SLOs for Baseline Workloads (internal targets used for gating)

- Short prompt (SEQ<=64, BATCH=1): p95_latency_ms < 120ms, p99_latency_ms < 220ms.
- Medium gen (SEQ=512, BATCH=4): tokens_per_second >= 2200 on 8xA100-80GB equiv, p95_latency_ms < 500ms.
- Long gen (SEQ=2048, BATCH<=1): tokens_per_second >= 250, sustained gpu_util_pct >= 70% for steady-state.
- Embeddings (batch=64, dim=1536-like): mean throughput >= 14k embeddings/sec on 4xA10-equivalent.

Workload Catalog (canonical names used in CI)

1) lm_short_start: config: MODEL_SHAPE=gpt2-like, SEQ=32, BATCH=1, PROMPT=512B. Purpose: cold-start latency and decoder head overhead profiling.
2) lm_medium_stream: MODEL_SHAPE=decoder-only, SEQ=512, BATCH=4, STREAM=on. Purpose: throughput under steady-state generation with KV-cache reuse.
3) lm_long_attention: MODEL_SHAPE=longformer-ish, SEQ=2048, BATCH=1, KV_CACHE=enabled. Purpose: test attention kernel scaling and KV cache eviction.
4) embed_bulk: MODEL_SHAPE=encoder-only, BATCH=64, SEQ=128. Purpose: dense matrix matmul stress and host-to-device IO patterns.
5) io_saturate: MODEL_SHAPE=small, SEQ=32, BATCH=32, MULTI_REGION=true. Purpose: simulate gateway aggregation and network bottlenecks.

Each canonical workload maps to a YAML presubmit harness in perf-ci (see "Presets" section). Naming must be stable: do not rename LM workloads without coordination with perf infra and dashboards.

Running Benchmarks Locally

Prereqs: access to perf infra bastion, `perf-bench` cli (version >= 1.12.0), k8s context set to perf cluster.

Example (short prompt):

$ perf-bench run \ 
  --preset=lm_short_start \ 
  --nodes=1 --gpus=1 \ 
  --collector=telemetry-prometheus \ 
  --output=/tmp/bench-lm_short_start.json

Example (long generation):

$ perf-bench run --preset=lm_long_attention --nodes=2 --gpus=4 --duration=600s --traces=enabled

Presets (perf-ci YAML names)

- presets/lm_short_start.yaml
- presets/lm_medium_stream.yaml
- presets/lm_long_attention.yaml
- presets/embed_bulk.yaml
- presets/io_saturate.yaml

Each preset contains a reproducible seed, tokenizer spec, model-architecture stub, and hardware probe mapping. The presets live in repo: infra/perf-harness/presets/. When adding presets, append a changelog entry in infra/perf-harness/CHANGELOG.md and include reviewer from perf infra.

Kernel Scheduler Tuning Matrix

Purpose: provide deterministic knob sets to test scheduler behaviors under different contention patterns. Matrix entries are applied via runtime config flag sets. Example knobs:

- scheduler.policy: {fair, latency-first, throughput-first}
- batch.max_tokens: integer (2048, 4096, 8192)
- batch.max_requests: integer (1,4,16)
- kernel.prefer_fp16_kernels: true|false
- kvcache.eviction_window_ms: 0|50|200

Sample matrix row (text table):

| scenario | scheduler.policy | batch.max_tokens | batch.max_requests | kernel.fp16 | kv_eviction_ms | expected 
| short-latency | latency-first | 2048 | 1 | true | 0 | minimize p95 
| throughput-burst | throughput-first | 8192 | 16 | true | 200 | maximize tokens/s under high concurrency
| mixed | fair | 4096 | 4 | false | 50 | balanced p95/p99 and throughput

How to apply a row in CI:

1) Create runtime-config overlay: runtime/config/overlays/<matrix-row>.yaml
2) Create perf-ci job: perf-ci/jobs/<matrix-row>-smoke.yaml referencing preset + runtime overlay.
3) Run presubmit: ./scripts/submit-perf-job.sh --job <matrix-row>-smoke
4) Collect metrics and compare against baseline using `perf-compare` tool.

Reproducibility and Normalization

- All runs must specify `--seed` and `--hardware-probe` (example: --hardware-probe=a100-80gb-8x).
- Normalize latency metrics to gateway-timestamp anchored traces; separate transport latency from kernel_exec_ms by using local-span markers (see instrumentation section below).
- Use the canonical baseline snapshot: baseline-2026-01-01 stored under gs://redwood-perf/baselines/baseline-20260101/ (includes preset config and golden traces).

Instrumentation & Tracing

- Ensure runtime is built with tracing enabled (env RUNTIME_TRACE=on) for benchmark runs unless specifically testing overhead.
- Span names: gateway.request, runtime.dispatch, kernel.exec.<kernel_name>, kvcache.hit, kvcache.miss, cuda.copy_h2d, cuda.copy_d2h.
- Prometheus exporters: runtime_exporter:9100, kernel_exporter:9400.

Perf CI Integration and Gating Rules

- Perf-CI has two lanes: nightly (full catalog) and presubmit (smoke). Presubmit jobs must pass the relevant SLOs for changed subsystems.
- Gating rule (kernel changes): any change to kernel/* or scheduler/* must pass the corresponding matrix-row smoke job with p95 degradation < 5% and no increase in error_rate_pct > 0.05%.
- Release gating for runtime minor releases: public release requires nightly baseline comparison with regression-free status and signed perf-release note from owner.

Release Notes Template (perf-specific)

- Title: runtime perf snapshot YYYY-MM-DD
- Summary: short bullets describing changes, e.g., kernel X rewrites, scheduler policy changes.
- Baseline: baseline-id used for comparison.
- Diffs: key metrics that changed (table format recommended).
- Risk: components with potential regression impact.
- Rollout recommendation: percentage canary, fallback policy, rollback steps.

Known Issues and Workarounds (living list)

- Issue: occasional p99 spikes on SEQ=2048 workloads after NVLINK driver update (2026-01-15).
  - Symptom: p99 increases by 30%-60% for bursts > 30s.
  - Mitigation: set runtime.env NVLINK_P2P_STRICT=false as a temporary rollback.
  - Owner: eng-serving-runtime/kernel-team.

- Issue: small-batch embeddings suffer from host-side memcpy stall on ubuntu-22-kv (2025-12-02).
  - Workaround: enable host-coalescing (runtime flag: host_io.coalesce=true) or use batch=16.
  - Owner: eng-serving-runtime/io-team.

- Issue: scheduler.metrics exporter intermittently drops kernel_exec_ms for sub-ms kernels when exporter load > 2000 series/s.
  - Workaround: throttle exporter scrape interval to 10s during heavy runs.
  - Owner: eng-serving-runtime/observability.

Runbook: Investigating a Perf Regression (short checklist)

1) Reproduce the failure with the canonical preset and baseline hardware probe. Use `perf-bench run --preset=<preset> --hardware-probe=<probe> --attempts=3`.
2) Collect traces and flamegraphs: upload to gs://redwood-perf/traces/<run-id>/ and call `perf-analyze <run-id> --report`.
3) Compare against baseline: `perf-compare --baseline baseline-20260101 --run <run-id> --metrics p95,p99,tokens_per_second`.
4) If kernel_exec_ms spike: file kernel-prof capture (`perf-kernel-capture --duration=30s --output /tmp/kernel.prof`) and open with kernel-ui.
5) If NVLINK or CUDA issues suspected: check nvidia-smi topo --matrix and dmesg for GPU driver warnings.
6) Engage owners: @kernel-team, @runtime-schedulers, @perf-infra. Tag ticket in JIRA: PERF-<component>-<date>.

Dashboards and Alerts

- Dashboards: runtime/perf-overview, runtime/kernel-latency, runtime/kvcache-stats. All dashboards show a 90-day trend baseline.
- Alerts: alert when p95 short-latency > 150ms for >10m, or when tokens_per_second drops by >25% vs 1h rolling median.

Ownership and Contact

- Document owner: eng-serving-runtime/perf (Anika Rao)
- Kernel team owner: eng-serving-runtime/kernel (Marcus Chen)
- Scheduler owner: eng-serving-runtime/schedulers (Lena Ortiz)
- Perf infra: infra/perf-harness team (perf-infra@redwood.example.com)

Appendix: Example runtime overlay (YAML snippet)

runtime_overlay: |
  runtime:
    scheduler:
      policy: latency-first
      batch:
        max_tokens: 2048
        max_requests: 1
    kernel:
      prefer_fp16_kernels: true
    kvcache:
      eviction_window_ms: 0

Glossary and References

- perf-bench: infra/perf-harness CLI used across CI and ad-hoc runs.
- perf-compare: tool that computes diffs and produces regression badges.
- baseline snapshots: gs://redwood-perf/baselines/
- Related: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook/runtime-profiling-playbook-guidelines-2025
